title: SEC confidential-treatment expiry / unsealing information state

hypothesis.mechanism: Public transitions in the confidentiality state of SEC-filed material contracts may reveal information previously withheld from the public, creating an information-acquisition state distinct from EDGAR demand, comment-letter dialogue, FOIA requests, and generic filing complexity.
hypothesis.event_clock: Only the first independently reproducible public SEC observation of the state transition is eligible; latent contractual/administrative expiry dates are not the trading clock unless the public record exposes them before the transition.

evidence_basis.finding: When a confidential treatment order approaches expiration, the registrant may refile the unredacted exhibit or seek an extension; extensions must be filed before expiry.

The traditional confidential-treatment process remains available, while post-2019 redacted-exhibit rules allow certain immaterial competitively harmful information to be omitted without a separate confidentiality request.

evidence_basis.source: Thompson, Urcan & Yoon (2023), The Accounting Review
evidence_basis.finding: Redacted material-contract filings are associated with slower stock-price discovery and greater insider trading; redaction became more frequent and insider trading more pronounced after the FAST Act.

evidence_basis.source: Kolev, Lee & Neamtiu (2023), Journal of Accounting and Public Policy
evidence_basis.finding: SEC confidential-treatment requests are associated with more intense SEC monitoring, more comment letters, and longer resolution processes; CT requests are observed in EDGAR for 2008–2017 in the study.

A public corpus contains more than one million SEC-filed contracts from 2000–2023, with filing metadata, document format and amendment status, indicating a potentially scalable historical contract/exhibit universe.

cheap_falsifiers: Historical public archive does not permit deterministic reconstruction of CTR approval, extension and unredacted-refile lineage.
The only usable clock is latent expiry rather than the first reproducibly public observation.
Post-2019 redacted-exhibit regime creates an unresolvable structural break for a unified sample.
Unredaction/extension events are too sparse for a stable issuer-level population.
Issuer or contract mapping requires hindsight or future outcomes.
The observable event collapses to Q218/Q224/Q228/Q231 or generic filing complexity under blinded ablation.
Recovered-content magnitude cannot be computed reproducibly without relying on non-public source material.
gates: historical SEC confidential-treatment order and exhibit-archive completeness
public observation-clock reconstruction for approval, extension and unredacted refiling
orthogonality audit against Q218, Q224, Q228 and Q231
independent PIT reproduction on issuer-disjoint sample

implementation_plan.phase_1: Source census only: enumerate historical CT ORDER and linked exhibit records; quantify clock and lineage completeness.
implementation_plan.phase_2: Deterministic state-transition compiler; freeze only public observation boundaries.
implementation_plan.phase_3: Cheap falsification and orthogonality; no return ranking.
implementation_plan.phase_4: Formal candidate admission only if all source/PIT gates pass.

status_note: This is a research lead generated from independently verified primary-source and peer-reviewed evidence. It is not yet in the formal candidate registry and carries no performance authorization.
